title: upgrade-attention-kernels-flashattnv2-rope-fused-ops-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Performance: Upgrades attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary ops and fused QKV paths. Improves throughput and latency, safe rollout behind feature flag.
body: Summary: This PR upgrades the serving runtime's attention implementation to use FlashAttentionV2 kernels with fused rotary/rope operations and fused QKV projection paths, and extends scheduler and continuous-batching logic to take advantage of the new kernels and consolidated KV cache layout. Motivation: recent benchmarks and production traces showed head-room for both throughput and memory reduction in long-context workloads. The previous FlashAttentionV1-based path had extra memory copies and separate rotary application which increased per-token overhead and limited effective batching. This change: 1) Integrates FlashAttentionV2 kernels (with optional fallback to v1 when unsupported) and selects fused-rope fused-QKV kernels when model config indicates rotary embeddings present. 2) Implements a consolidated KV cache layout that reduces scatter/gather copies when sharding or moving KV between GPUs. 3) Adds kernel-aware continuous-batching hints to the scheduler so batching decisions prefer batch shapes that the new kernels handle more efficiently (reduces kernel launch overhead and improves utilization). 4) Adds an autotuning pass at startup to pick the best kernel variant for the detected GPU and sequence length distribution. 5) Adds feature flags and rollout gate: runtime flag flashattn_v2_enabled, and per-customer rollout via routing policy. Compatibility: preserves model correctness and numeric results within expected tolerance. Fallbacks to previous kernel path are available on GPUs without required SM capabilities or when autotuner detects regressions. Testing: unit tests for fused rotary logic, KV cache consistency checks, new e2e perf test harness entries, and an integration canary run on a dedicated pool. Migration/rollout: default-off for hosted until canary completes; enabled on dedicated and private deployments via config. See perf_summary for numbers. Checklist: - [x] Kernel integration and build changes - [x] KV cache layout changes + tests - [x] Scheduler hints + autotuner - [x] Feature flags + rollout gating - [x] Benchmarks and canary runs - [x] Docs updated (release notes and runtime flags) Related: references ENG-8421 (attention perf), prior PRs pr-61234 and pr-67239 which started FlashAttentionV2 experiments.

review_comments: Evelyn Park: Overall this looks great. A couple of nits around error handling in the fallback path and an additional KV consistency check would be good.
Ava Patel: Addressed the nits, added an extra consistency assertion and updated comments explaining the layout.
Lucas Ng: Can you add a small microbenchmark for 4k tokens on A100 and H100 and include p50/p95? Also prefer feature flag default-off for hosted.
Ava Patel: Added microbench results and made hosted default-off. Confirmed autotuner will enable for Dedicated when allowed by config.
Priya Sharma: Verified tests and canary results on dedicated pool are green. Approval pending one CI re-run.

CI Bot: All checks passed after rerun.
perf_summary: Microbench (A100, fp16, batch=8, seq=2048): +22% throughput, p50 latency -18%
Microbench (H100, fp16, batch=16, seq=4096): +28% throughput, p50 latency -24%
End-to-end canary (dedicated pool, mixed workloads): average tokens/sec +15%, memory footprint -12% for long-context models
KV copy reduction: 30-40% fewer device-host-device copies observed in pathway when sharding or migrating KV
Observed worst-case numeric drift: < 1e-4 on fp16 workloads compared to baseline v1 path
notes: Rollout: gated behind runtime flag 'flashattn_v2_enabled' and per-customer routing policies. Will enable by default after 2 weeks of canary on hosted and broader Dedicated rollout.
Operational: added alert 'flashattn_v2_kernel_errors' and dashboard tiles for kernel fallback rates and autotuner choices.
Follow-ups: ENG-8702 to optimize small-batch shapes and ENG-8745 to upstream some kernel changes to open-source wrapper.
